rows.subtype: Approach: rebuild with documents, insurance and mental-health support [Revision]
rows.description: After the disaster, the person applies for relief, files an insurance claim with photos, replaces lost papers and speaks to a counsellor about stress. Recovery is planned in stages.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: constraint-based thinking, contingency planning, forward planning, mental simulation, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: rehearse an earthquake drill at home [Thinking]
rows.description: The student practises drop, cover and hold on and identifies a sturdy table and exits, and teaches younger siblings. Rehearsal turns a panic reaction into a learned response.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: constraint-based thinking, contingency planning, forward planning, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: ration supplies and check on stranded relatives [Revision]
rows.description: Trapped by floods for two days, the person counts food and water, plans consumption and contacts relatives by any working channel. Replanning to constraints helps stretch resources.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: contingency planning, forward planning, mental simulation, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: notice the warning signs of pressure and isolation [Thinking]
rows.description: A student invited to a friendly self-improvement group sees that leaders discourage contact with family, demand large payments and label doubters as weak. Recognising these patterns creates distance.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: seeking advice, sleeping on it, values-first planning

rows.subtype: Approach: keep outside relationships and reality checks [Action]
rows.description: The person continues weekly calls with family and old friends, and discusses what the group says with them. Outside views break the closed loop that such groups depend on.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: seeking advice, sleeping on it, values-first planning

rows.subtype: Approach: commit gradually because each step seemed small [Pitfall]
rows.description: First a free workshop, then donations, then leaving college for group work. Each small step feels consistent with the last, and the escalation of commitment makes leaving harder.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: seeking advice, sleeping on it, values-first planning

rows.subtype: Approach: set limits on time and money in advance [Action]
rows.description: Before attending, the person decides a maximum time per week, no financial commitments and no signing of papers on the spot. A pre-set limit is harder to erode in the moment.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: seeking advice, sleeping on it, values-first planning

rows.subtype: Approach: ask for details and independent information [Thinking]
rows.description: The person asks where funds go, who leads and what former members say, and looks up news and reviews. A group that resists questions signals a problem.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: seeking advice, sleeping on it, values-first planning

rows.subtype: Approach: give in to social pressure to belong [Pitfall]
rows.description: Lonely in a new city, the person values the warm welcome and love bombing and ignores doubts. The need for belonging outweighs judgement, and the person reads doubt as personal failure.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: seeking advice, sleeping on it
related mind states: affection, doubt, loneliness, nostalgia

rows.subtype: Approach: step away with support and a safe exit plan [Revision]
rows.description: Feeling uneasy, the person tells a trusted friend, avoids private meetings with leaders, and stops attending, leaning on family and, if threatened, the police. Leaving is planned with support.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: seeking advice, values-first planning
